catalog_quote: Kadu is one of the many tonal languages spoken in Southeast Asia. ... The Kadu language tonal system falls into the first category. The three tonemic distinctions occurring in Kadu involve three pitch registers. ... This thesis proposes that Kadu has phonemic contrasts between high, mid, and low tones occurring on all vowels and on all syllable types. ... Mid tone is the most common tone in this language. ... This section presents two types of syllable structures attested in Kadu: major and minor (also called strong and weak) syllables. Major syllables are those capable of functioning as major word classes such as nouns and verbs. The major syllables have more complex nuclei and contrastive tones. sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke (藤原敬介). 2020. モーラン・カドゥー語音韻論の概要 [An overview of Molang Kadu phonology]. 京都大学言語学研究 (Kyoto University Linguistic Research) 39: 47-65. DOI 10.14989/261912.
sources.quote: '声調：四声調（高声調、中声調、低声調、下降（緊喉）声調）であり、固有の声調をもたない軽声として /ə/ がある。軽声は開音節のみであらわれるけれども、語の最終音節にはあらわれない。他の声調は、すべての音節構造であらわれうる。' [Tone: four tones (high, mid, low, falling/creaky), plus a light syllable /ə/ with no inherent tone; the light syllable occurs only in open syllables and never word-finally; the other tones can occur on every syllable type.] No stress statement.
sources.locator: abstract item 2 p. 47; sec. 2.2 item c p. 50 (pdf p. 4)
sources.note: Most recent phonology of a Kadu variety (Molang); explicit statement that /ə/ light syllable has no inherent tone and never occurs word-finally — confirms sesquisyllabic tonal profile with no stress rule.

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke (藤原敬介). 2013. カドゥー語音韻論 [Kadu Phonology]. 東南アジア研究 (Japanese Journal of Southeast Asian Studies) 51(1): 3-33. DOI 10.20495/tak.51.1_3.
sources.quote: 'カドゥー語では声調は音節単位で付与されるとかんがえる。(21)にしめす四声調が弁別的である' [In Kadu, tone is considered to be assigned syllable by syllable; the four tones in (21) — high, mid, low, falling — are distinctive]; 'ə は軽声をになう音節（CəC-）にのみあらわれる' [ə occurs only in light/toneless syllables CəC-]; sesquisyllabic words CəCV(V)(C) are frequent; sec. III.3.1 '軽声そのものは変調に関与しない' [the toneless syllable itself plays no part in tone sandhi]. No mention of 強勢/ストレス (stress) anywhere in the 31 pages.
sources.locator: sec. III.1.1 p. 16 (pdf p. 14); sec. II vowel notes p. 7-8; abstract p. 3
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology article on (Settau) Kadu; record cited the grammar alone. fetched sources: tone per syllable, toneless minor syllable, no stress — confirms; could be added as a corroborating source (notes 4 tones vs Sangdong's 3).

sources.citation: Huziwara, Keisuke (藤原敬介). 2012. ガナン語音韻論 [Ganan phonology]. 大阪大学世界言語研究センター論集 (RIWL, Osaka University) 7: 121-144. hdl 11094/5146. (Glottolog ref 548871; Ganaan dialect gana1267 of kado1242.)
sources.quote: 'ガナン語では声調は音節単位で付与されるとかんがえる。(19)にしめす三声調が弁別的' [In Ganan tone is assigned per syllable; three tones (high, mid, low) are distinctive]; 'ə は軽声（CəC-）としてのみあらわれる' [ə appears only as a toneless light syllable]; sesquisyllabic words frequent. No stress statement. Covers the sister dialect under the same Glottolog language; same prosodic type.
